messages:
elaine: Heads up — nightly perf run shows a ~22% tail latency regression for fp8 small-batch workloads on sm86 after yesterday's runtime compile changes :grimacing:
omar: repro able locally? which config/commit?
elaine: yes, repro on a single p4d (sm86) VM. commit 4f9a2b3 flipped CUTLASS kernel selector + enabled kv-prefetch heuristic. nvprof snapshot attached in thread (pasted below).
omar: can you paste the short perf diff (p50/p95/p99) and the failing test name?
elaine: p50: 8ms -> 9ms, p95: 24ms -> 31ms, p99: 48ms -> 59ms on chat-generate-smallbatch (batch=1-4, seq=128). test: perf/chat_generate_fp8_prefetch_smallbatch
tess: interesting — selector may be preferring a CUTLASS int8-path rather than the fp8 fused kernel because of minor changes in sm_efficiency heuristics. did calibration toggle change?
elaine: not explicitly. but the calibration routine (autocalib) now runs earlier in the compile pipeline (new ordering in build flags). that bumped the runtime decision table entries.
harry: paste nvprof block?
elaine: ```
== Kernel: cutlass_gemm_int8
  time  : 12.3ms
  gld   : 1.4GB
== Kernel: rwd_fp8_fused_attention
  time  : 6.1ms
  gld   : 2.8GB
== Kernel: cutlass_gemm_fp8_fallback
  time  : 10.8ms
  gld   : 3.1GB
```
ben: wait, fp8 fused attention is faster per-kernel but GLD doubled — looks like more global memory thrash (KV prefetch may be duplicating loads). when sequence is short the selector should prefer fused small-KV path, but I guess prefetch expands the working set.
omar: can you run with REDWOOD_PROBER=1 and TRITON_FORCE_CUTLASS=0 to force-trace kernel selection? also run with REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0 to compare.
elaine: done. with prefetch=0 the p95 drops back to 25ms. with TRITON_FORCE_CUTLASS=0 we get the fused fp8 kernel consistently and throughput recovers.
tess: that suggests an interaction: builder/arch-detect sets SM flag->CUTLASS path + kv-prefetch inflates cache footprint -> increases GLD and stalls. maybe the new build flag -DENABLE_CUTLASS_ARCH_FALLBACK=ON made the selector prefer CUTLASS on sm86.
harry: quick fix option: gate kv-prefetch for batch<=4 or seq<=160 on sm86 until we root cause. cheaper than revert.
ben: agree. also drop-in experiment: set runtime override `selector.prefer_fused_fp8=true` and run 5 runs to validate.
ci-bot: ci/perf-nightly #1851: flaky tests flagged: perf/chat_generate_fp8_prefetch_smallbatch failed regression threshold. See: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/1851
elaine: I'm going to push a canary: disable kv-prefetch for small-batches on sm86 + explicit selector override. I'll annotate the PR with perf traces and the commit to revert later (4f9a2b3).
omar: +1. also open a follow-up to add a unit test that asserts kernel-selection invariants for batch=1..4 so we don't silently flip.
tess: and add a microbenchmark that measures GLD bytes / kernel choice distribution — then alert if GLD increases >10% for the same model.
harry: logging the action items: 1) canary PR (disable prefetch for small-batch on sm86) — elaine 2) selector override runtime flag — ben 3) repro harness + selector unit test — omar 4) add GLD guard metric to perf-nightly — tess
elaine: will open PRs now, linking traces and nvprof outputs. tagging you all in reviews :pray: 
ben: thanks — cc perf-oncall if this hits customer infra.
essentials-note: keep an eye on dedicated pools — this reg only surfaced under bursty small-batch traffic.
